QUOTE: The one documented way to get direct access is to define `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` before including mbedtls headers... By default, a struct member written as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)` is declared and named `private_state`... `library/common.h:132` defines `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` unconditionally... so the library's translation units see the real member names.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that code defining the opt-out sees real member names while default consumers of the public headers see `private_*` names.
